Social technology assessment (STa) can be a crucial tool for measuring technology management complexity (TMC). By scrutinizing the social dynamics of technological systems, STa can help identify clusters of interconnected components that contribute to TMC. To quantify TMC, STa can employ various metrics, such as the complexity of social networks (CSN), which measures the number of clusters, modularity, and community structure. Additionally, the assessment can evaluate the effectiveness of technology management strategies (TMS) by analyzing their impact on TMC. This can involve assessing the complexity of decision-making processes, the level of coordination required among stakeholders, and the degree of adaptability needed to respond to changing technological landscapes.

Furthermore, STa can help identify potential hotspots of complexity within technological systems, which can inform targeted interventions to mitigate TMC. By analyzing the social and technical dynamics of these hotspots, technology managers can develop more effective strategies to simplify complex systems, reduce uncertainty, and improve overall system performance.

In conclusion, social technology assessment can be a powerful tool for measuring technology management complexity, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the intricate social and technical dynamics that underlie complex technological systems. By leveraging STa, technology managers can develop more effective strategies to manage complexity, improve system performance, and drive innovation in the digital age.
